old: It's built from two old Greek pieces — one meaning existence, one meaning the act of setting marks down.
Break it apart and you get 'life' plus 'writing,' straight from Greek.
It passed through New Latin before landing in English, keeping its Greek roots βίος and -γραφία intact.
clues: This kind of nonfiction book has a name built partly from an ancient Greek root meaning writing, the same root behind many English words.
It tells the true story of a real person's life, usually written by someone else, unlike a memoir. Fittingly, its first ancient Greek root meant life.
An authorized one is written with its subject's cooperation, and Walter Isaacson wrote famous ones about Steve Jobs and Albert Einstein.
